summary.title: A list of programming playgrounds
summary.one_liner: A curated list of online "playground" tools for quickly experimenting with compilers, CSS/HTML/JS, SQL, DNS, data formats, and programming languages in the browser.
takeaways: Browser-based playgrounds exist for many domains: compilers, shaders, Arduino/IoT, CSS/HTML/JS, DNS, nginx, SQL, Postgres, and Git.
Some playgrounds bytecode and language internals, such as SharpLab for .NET and dis this for Python bytecode.
Data-format tools cover floating point, Unicode, ASN.1 certificates, SVG, CBOR, JSON, and cron expressions.
Language-specific playgrounds include 3v4l for PHP, Python Tutor for step-through execution, jqplay for jq, and tryapl for APL.
summary.summary: This blog post by Julia Evans is a categorized list of programming playgrounds, collected after she asked for suggestions on Mastodon. Entries are grouped by topic (compilers, shaders, CSS/HTML/JS, DNS, SQL, data formats, programming languages) and each names the tool and its creator. The page gives no detailed descriptions beyond short notes, so it works mainly as a directory of links to explore. Some sections, such as official and unofficial language playgrounds and regular expressions, are left empty in the list.
